items.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: Oh yes. Oh yes. Because the music of the white musicians that you’re mentioning there was actually released far more widely in Europe than was that of the black Americans perhaps. Those records were widely known.

ctx.x: Put it in words for me if you can, what made them so distinguishable?

The energy, which is still a powerful factor to me; the rhythmic drive; and just that sense that something was kind of bursting out of the grooves that was quite unlike anything else. To me then, Beiderbecke and Trumbauer seemed effete. All right? A little restrained. I like that sense of, you know, all out emotion. I think it was the emotion in other words. And I suppose by then I’d started to read a lot, you know I’d read Louis’ autobiography by then. I’d read Bechet’s autobiography. I’d read, Rudi Blesh’s…
Yeah. You got to a point where you actually could make a living as a writer?
